Frequently Asked Questions (Postgres Cloud Cost Calculator)

Why is AWS RDS often significantly more expensive than Supabase or Neon for startups?

AWS RDS bills separately for every component: instance hours ($0.154+/hr for db.m6g.large), provisioned gp3 storage ($0.115/GB), provisioned IOPS beyond 3000 ($0.02/IOPS), automated snapshots ($0.095/GB), and internet egress ($0.09/GB). In contrast, Supabase Pro bundles 8 GB storage, 50 GB egress, daily backups, and pgvector for a flat $25/month base fee.

How does Neon Serverless PostgreSQL handle auto-suspend and scale-to-zero?

Neon separates compute from storage. When an endpoint receives zero incoming connection queries for a configurable timeout (typically 5 minutes), the compute container automatically suspends. Storage remains persistent at $0.175/GB-mo. When a new query arrives, Neon wakes up within ~500ms, saving up to 80% on dev, test, and staging environments.

Does Supabase include connection pooling and pgvector out of the box?

Yes. Every Supabase PostgreSQL database includes built-in Supavisor connection pooling (handling tens of thousands of client connections without exhausting database RAM) and pre-installed extensions including pgvector for AI embedding search, PostGIS for geospatial data, and Row-Level Security (RLS).
